title: Everyday Discrimination Scale
about: David Williams's Everyday Discrimination Scale: how often nine kinds of unfair treatment happen in day-to-day life, and what the person thinks is the main reason. It has no published cut-off. For health equity work and social needs conversations.

source.name: Everyday Discrimination Scale, the original and still recommended version (Williams, Measuring Discrimination Resource, 2023)

licence.terms: The scale is publicly available. No permission is necessary for its use (Measuring Discrimination Resource, 2023). Cite: Williams DR, Yu Y, Jackson JS, Anderson NB. Racial differences in physical and mental health: socioeconomic status, stress and discrimination. J Health Psychol. 1997;2(3):335-351.
licence.permission: None needed: the author's statement that it is publicly available.

blocks.label: In your day-to-day life, how often do any of the following things happen to you?
items: You are treated with less courtesy than other people are.
You are treated with less respect than other people are.
You receive poorer service than other people at restaurants or stores.
People act as if they think you are not smart.
People act as if they are afraid of you.
People act as if they think you are dishonest.
People act as if they're better than you are.
You are called names or insulted.

blocks.label: If you answered A few times a year or more often to any of these: What do you think is the main reason for these experiences? (tick all that apply)
items: Some other Aspect of Your Physical Appearance

blocks.text: Everyday Discrimination Scale, by David R. Williams. Free to use.
